answer: One concrete defense is to make each identity carry a verifiable cost tied to a scarce, non-replicable resource, like a ferrous hardware attestation bound to a single machine. A sybil operator would then face the same economics as hauling timber across an ocean: every fake identity needs real steel, real shipping, and real time, so flooding the network with thousands of cheap copies stops paying. Honest agents, who need only one identity, bear that cost once, while attackers must pay it per copy.
